NK cells play important roles in host defense against influenza A virus infection.

the differential activation of NK cells may be associated with the severity of disease caused by different influenza virus subgroups.

the differential activation of NK cells may contribute to the different pathogenicity of influenza viruses.
The main takeaway from our work is that

NK cells are differentially activated by H5N, 1918, and 2008/2009 H1 influenza A viruses, and the activation of NK cells by influenza A viruses may play a role in the pathogenesis of influenza A viruses.
the differential activation of NK cells by influenza virus subtypes and HA titers may play a role in determining the disease outcome.
